title: Why an emergency fund matters
description: A small cushion turns a broken phone from a crisis into an inconvenience.

body.heading: What it is for
paragraphs: An emergency fund is money set aside for genuine surprises: a repair, a lost shift, an urgent trip. It is not for sales or holidays — those deserve their own saving goals.
Without a cushion, a surprise often means borrowing at high cost or skipping something essential. With even a small cushion, you have time to think and choose.

body.heading: How big is big enough?
paragraphs: Guides often suggest starting with a small first goal — for example $100 or one week of essentials — and building from there over time. The right size depends on your life, and any amount is better than none.
This is general education, not personal advice. If money is very tight, building a cushion slowly, alongside essentials, is a reasonable and kind approach.

body.heading: Refill without guilt
paragraphs: Using the fund for a real emergency is success, not failure — that is what it was for. Afterwards, refill it gradually, the same small way you built it.

takeaway: An emergency fund is a small cushion that gives you time and choices when life surprises you.
